claims.claim: Ouster completed the StereoLabs acquisition in February 2026, adding stereo cameras, AI compute, sensor fusion and perception software to digital lidar.
StereoLabs had shipped more than 90,000 ZED cameras to over 10,000 customers, broadening Ouster's developer and customer surface beyond lidar.
Ouster later announced a strategic agreement with AIM Intelligent Machines for lidar on AI-powered heavy earthmoving equipment.

factors.name: physical-AI platform breadth
factors.basis: Combined lidar, vision, compute and perception software expands the addressable sensing stack.

factors.name: robotics/heavy-industry pull
factors.basis: AIM agreement provides application-level evidence in autonomous heavy equipment.

risks.risk: Acquisition integration and multi-sensor platform complexity can raise execution costs and dilute focus.

unknowns.unknown: Revenue scale and margins attributable to StereoLabs after integration are not isolated in these sources.

claims.claim: First-quarter 2026 product revenue was $48 million, up 55% year over year, with more than 12,600 lidar and camera sensors shipped; GAAP gross margin was 43% and adjusted EBITDA remained a $7 million loss.
The quarter showed strong product growth but not yet sustained profitability, making margin and EBITDA conversion an important execution test.

factors.name: product growth
factors.basis: 55% year-over-year product revenue growth and higher unit shipments show operating demand expansion.

factors.name: profitability conversion
factors.basis: Gross margin improved year over year while adjusted EBITDA remained negative.

risks.risk: Prior-quarter royalty revenue was largely one-time, so headline sequential revenue comparisons can misstate underlying product trajectory.

unknowns.unknown: Later-quarter profitability and integration outcomes require newer financial evidence from Alpha.
